title: Physical Constraints on Latency and Energy Use in Biological and Artificial Information Processing
plain_title: How fast and how cheaply can brains and chips compute?
thesis: Brains and computers are governed by the same transport delays and heat limits, and when you compare on-chip compute to local synapses the energy gap is about 71 times — whereas moving data off-chip to DRAM opens a 20,000-fold chasm.
summary: The paper benchmarks all 33 physical and biological substrates in the project's hardware table across 68 census moments — from bacterial chemotaxis, cortical synapses and giant squid axons to Nvidia GPUs, photonic accelerators and 4.2-kelvin superconducting logic. It separates ballistic and cable propagation from square-law chemical diffusion, shows why the Landauer bit-erasure floor sits 19 orders of magnitude faster than millisecond neural integration, compares local synaptic currents (0.01 pJ) and amortized whole-brain synaptic budgets (0.133 pJ) against CMOS and cryogenic hardware, and evaluates neural power and brain-body scaling directly on the project's empirical tables.

claims.claim: A local cortical postsynaptic event is 70.9 times more energy efficient than a dense 16-bit operation on an Nvidia H100 — and 20,000 times more efficient than an off-chip HBM3 DRAM fetch.
claims.paper_value: local synapse 0.010 pJ (1.00×10¹⁴ events/J; whole-brain amortized human budget 0.133 pJ = 7.50×10¹² SynOps/J) vs H100 dense 1.41×10¹² ops/J (70.9× local, 5.32× amortized), B200 4.50×10¹² (22.2×), Apple M4 NPU 7.60×10¹² (13.2× local, 0.99× amortized parity), and HBM3 DRAM fetch 5.00×10⁹ ops/J (20,000× local)
claims.data_value: 70.9× vs H100 dense, 22.2× vs B200, 13.2× vs M4 NPU, and 20,000× vs HBM3 DRAM in cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv
claims.source: cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv (cortical synapse, H100 dense, B200, M4 NPU, and HBM3 DRAM rows); Attwell and Laughlin 2001
claims.note: Revised on 24 November 2026: both the local postsynaptic cleft cost (0.010 pJ) and the whole-brain amortized synaptic cost (0.133 pJ) are reported alongside the exact 20,000× DRAM ratio.

claims.claim: Superconducting AQFP logic cooled to 4.2 kelvin still beats every biological and room-temperature substrate after paying a ~400-to-1 Carnot + cryocooler wall-plug penalty.
claims.paper_value: 7.14×10¹⁹ ops/J intrinsic at 4.2 K; 1.79×10¹⁷ ops/J wall-plug after 400× cooling overhead = 1,790× above a local cortical synapse
claims.data_value: Carnot + 17.5% cryocooler efficiency gives ~402 W cooling per W cold dissipation; 7.14×10¹⁹ ÷ 400 = 1.79×10¹⁷ ops/J; ÷ 1.00×10¹⁴ = 1,790×
claims.note: Every step of the cryogenic Carnot chain and the 1,790× lead over cortical synapses reproduces cleanly.

claims.claim: Wall-plug cooled AQFP logic exceeds the most efficient room-temperature CMOS chips in the benchmark table by 2.36×10⁴ to 1.27×10⁵ times (4.4 to 5.1 orders of magnitude).
claims.paper_value: 2.36×10⁴× vs Apple M4 NPU (7.60×10¹² ops/J), 2.33×10⁴× vs Intel Hala Point (7.69×10¹²), 3.98×10⁴× vs Nvidia B200 (4.50×10¹²), and 1.27×10⁵× vs Nvidia H100 (1.41×10¹²)
claims.note: Revised on 24 November 2026: ratios are now given explicitly against the M4 NPU, Hala Point, B200 and H100 rather than treating H100 as the room-temperature CMOS ceiling.

claims.claim: Table 1 prints all 33 substrates verbatim from the canonical hardware benchmark table, including the electric-fish pacemaker cycle, dragonfly target-selective neuron and Apple M4 Neural Engine.
claims.paper_value: all 33 rows printed verbatim: electric fish 2.0 mm, 1.0 ms full 1 kHz cycle (vs 0.16–0.20 µs phase jitter in text), 5.00×10⁹ ops/J; dragonfly TSDN 4.0 mm, 25 ms, 8.00×10⁶ ops/J; Apple M4 NPU 5.0 W, 0.444 ns, 7.60×10¹² ops/J (7.6 TOPS/W at 1 MAC/op)
claims.data_value: exact row-for-row and column-for-column match across all 33 rows of cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv
claims.note: Revised on 24 November 2026: all 33 substrates appear in Table 1 and match the CSV identically.

claims.claim: Across all 33 substrates, operational latency spans 14.8 orders of magnitude and energy efficiency spans 14.2 orders of magnitude.
claims.paper_value: 14.81 orders in latency (2.13×10⁻¹¹ s RSFQ to 1.36×10⁴ s DNA Fountain) and 14.22 orders in efficiency (4.35×10⁵ ops/J blowfly haltere reflex to 7.14×10¹⁹ ops/J intrinsic AQFP; 11.6 orders wall-plug)
claims.source: cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv min and max across all 33 rows
claims.note: Both dynamic ranges match the full 33-row benchmark file to two decimal places.

claims.claim: Pure Fickian glutamate diffusion across a 20-nanometre synaptic cleft takes 0.263 microseconds, whereas the 200-to-300-microsecond canonical synaptic delay reflects vesicle exocytosis and receptor gating.
claims.paper_value: τ_diff = (20 nm)² ÷ (2 × 0.76 µm²/ms) = 0.263 µs pure cleft transit, embedded inside ~200–300 µs total Ca²⁺-SNARE release and AMPA gating delay
claims.data_value: (2×10⁻⁸ m)² ÷ (2 × 7.6×10⁻¹⁰ m²/s) = 2.63×10⁻⁷ s = 0.263 µs; hardware row transport/gating delay 2.0×10⁻⁴ s
claims.source: Analytical Fickian diffusion equation and cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv synapse row
claims.note: Revised on 24 November 2026: pure molecular cleft transit (0.263 µs) and vesicular release kinetics (200 µs) are cleanly separated in both prose and Figure 1.

claims.claim: Across the 23 canonical individual nervous systems in the neural evolution table, whole-brain metabolic power scales nearly linearly with neuron count (exponent 1.04 ± 0.08), matching the 2.3×10⁻¹⁰ W per mammalian neuron budget.
claims.paper_value: log10(P_brain) = (−9.23 ± 0.68) + (1.042 ± 0.083) × log10(N_neurons), R² = 0.882 across N = 23 canonical nervous systems; mammalian linear rule 2.3×10⁻¹⁰ W/neuron × 8.6×10¹⁰ = 19.8 W human brain
claims.data_value: OLS on neural_sensory_evolution_timeseries.csv (N = 23): slope 1.042 ± 0.083, intercept −9.23 ± 0.68, R² = 0.882; 8.6×10¹⁰ × 2.3×10⁻¹⁰ = 19.78 W
claims.note: Revised on 24 November 2026: regressed directly on neural_sensory_evolution_timeseries.csv and paired with Herculano-Houzel's measured 230 picowatts per mammalian neuron.

claims.claim: Across the 176 individual animal species in the biological catalog, brain mass scales with body mass (in grams) with slope 0.886 ± 0.029 (R² = 0.840).
claims.paper_value: N = 176 individual animals: log10(M_brain,g) = −2.0502 + (0.8859 ± 0.0293) × log10(M_body,g), R² = 0.8402 (all N = 277 positive-mass rows including collectives and synthetic rows: slope 0.7955 ± 0.0411, intercept −1.9630, R² = 0.5764)
claims.data_value: identical slopes, intercepts, standard errors and R² values recomputed from cleaned_biological_species.csv
claims.note: Revised on 24 November 2026: text, stats macros and Figure 4 all report the exact gram-unit OLS fits for both the filtered 176-animal set and the full 277-row table.

claims.claim: Prokaryotic single-cell power spans five orders of magnitude across metabolic states, from 556 femtowatts in rich-medium dividing E. coli down to 1 attowatt in deep subseafloor sediments.
claims.paper_value: 5.56×10⁻¹³ W (rich-medium dividing E. coli, 10⁻⁹ J ÷ 1,800 s), 1.0×10⁻¹⁵ W (chemotaxis rotary motor + receptor cluster), 2.03×10⁻¹⁷ W (field surface prokaryote mean), 2.00×10⁻¹⁸ W (oligotrophic standby), and 1.00×10⁻¹⁸ W (deep subseafloor basal maintenance)
claims.data_value: 1.0×10⁻⁹ ÷ 1,800 = 5.56×10⁻¹³ W; 1.0×10⁻¹⁵ W in cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv; 2.03×10⁻¹⁷, 2.00×10⁻¹⁸ and 1.00×10⁻¹⁸ W in paper0_power_closure_ledger.csv
claims.source: Lynch and Marinov 2015; Hoehler and Jørgensen 2013; cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv; paper0_power_closure_ledger.csv
claims.note: Distinguishing rich-medium division, sensory-motor chemotaxis and the three Paper 0 field compartments closes the prokaryotic bioenergetics cleanly.

claims.claim: Paracrine calcium waves across a 1-millimetre placozoan (Trichoplax) at 150 micrometres per second require 6.7 seconds for whole-body coordination, whereas myelinated vertebrate axons cut metre-scale transit to milliseconds.
claims.paper_value: 1.0 mm ÷ 0.15 mm/s = 6.7 s across a whole Trichoplax (0.67 s across a 100 µm patch), vs ~10 ms along a 1 m myelinated axon at 100 m/s
claims.note: All transport times now follow distance ÷ speed consistently across prose and figures.

rationale.step: Signal latency is bounded below by path length divided by propagation speed (or length squared over diffusivity for passive chemical diffusion).
rationale.note: Every example in the text, Table 1 and Figure 1 — cleft diffusion (0.263 µs), placozoan waves (6.7 s), electric-fish cycle (1.0 ms) and axons — obeys the transport equations.

rationale.step: At 300 K, the Landauer bit-erasure floor sits ~11 orders of magnitude in energy below a cortical synapse and 19 orders in export time below millisecond neural integration, so practical limits come from capacitance, ionic pumps and heat removal.
rationale.note: Both 2.87×10⁻²¹ J and 1.44×10⁻²² s (19 orders below 1 ms) reproduce accurately.

rationale.step: Comparing on-chip 16-bit compute to a local synapse yields a 71× gap (5.3× against whole-brain amortized cost), whereas off-chip DRAM movement opens a 20,000× gap.
rationale.note: Separating arithmetic energy from memory-traffic energy explains why data movement, not transistor switching alone, dominates AI power.

rationale.step: Adiabatic superconducting logic at 4.2 K achieves a 1,790× wall-plug efficiency lead over synapses and a 24,000× to 127,000× lead over room-temperature CMOS after paying the 400× refrigeration tax.
rationale.note: Verified against every CMOS row in the 33-substrate table, while noting cryogenic laboratory maturity limits.

rationale.step: Across animal species, whole-brain power scales nearly isometrically with neuron count (~230 pW per mammalian neuron) while pooled brain-body allometry masks the clade grade shifts analysed in Paper 2.
rationale.note: Both regressions reproduce directly from neural_sensory_evolution_timeseries.csv and cleaned_biological_species.csv.

conclusions.conclusion: On-chip GPU arithmetic sits within 71-fold of local cortical synaptic energy (and 5.3-fold of amortized whole-brain synaptic cost), whereas off-chip DRAM movement is 20,000 times costlier than a synapse.
conclusions.note: Directly verified in cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv, with operation-type differences explicitly noted.

conclusions.conclusion: Wall-plug 4.2 K adiabatic superconducting logic beats cortical synapses by 1,790× and the best room-temperature CMOS accelerators by 2.4×10⁴× to 1.3×10⁵× in laboratory circuit benchmarks.
conclusions.note: Follows directly from the 400× Carnot-cryocooler penalty and the 33-substrate table.

conclusions.conclusion: Myelination, saltatory conduction and 3D cortical folding evolved under strict transport-time and wiring-volume physics rather than Landauer bit-erasure limits.
conclusions.note: All physical time constants and geometric bounds check out cleanly.

conclusions.conclusion: Whole-brain metabolic power tracks total neuron count nearly linearly across animals, rising from ~0.06% to 20% of resting body metabolism (~312-fold).
conclusions.note: Reproduced on the 23-system neural power dataset and Herculano-Houzel 2011.

bottom_line: Following the 24 November 2026 revision, all 33 rows of Table 1, the 14.8-order latency and 14.2-order efficiency spans, synaptic-to-GPU/DRAM/AQFP efficiency ratios, Fickian cleft diffusion (0.263 µs), Landauer exponents (19 orders), five-state prokaryotic power regimes, neural power scaling (slope 1.04, R² = 0.88), gram-unit brain-body regressions (N = 176 and N = 277), catalog IDs and Figures 1–5 agree with the project's canonical data files.
revised: On 24 November 2026, Table 1 was expanded to all 33 canonical rows verbatim from cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv, synaptic-to-DRAM (20,000×) and AQFP-to-CMOS (2.36×10⁴× to 1.27×10⁵×) ratios were reconciled, pure cleft diffusion (0.263 µs) was separated from vesicular delay (200 µs), neural power and gram-unit brain-body regressions were recomputed directly from the canonical CSVs, prokaryotic power states and catalog IDs were aligned, and all five figures were regenerated.
